author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory can be narrowed to one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian directory surfaces accept an optional specialty and list only the veterinarians holding it. The name is matched whole and case-insensitively; no specialty asked for leaves today's behavior untouched.
acceptance_criteria: given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the directory page is narrowed to it, then only those veterinarians are listed, a page at a time over the narrowed list
given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the machine-readable directory is narrowed to it, then it carries only those veterinarians
given no specialty asked for, when either surface is opened, then it behaves as it did before narrowing existed
edge case 2: a specialty name differing from the held specialty only by letter case matches it, on either surface
edge case 3: only the whole specialty name matches; the opening letters of a name match nothing
edge case 4: a specialty no veterinarian holds returns the ordinary page or document with no veterinarian in it, on either surface, and neither a failure nor a 'nothing found' message
edge case 5: a specialty asked for as an empty value, or as spaces alone, behaves as if none had been asked for, mirroring an empty owner search
non_goals: free-text veterinarian search: NG-9 still declines matching typed-in text against stored names
narrowing the directory by any attribute other than specialty
managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2)
notes: NG-9 narrowed 2026-08-04; the decision trail is docs/adr/2026-08-04-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md. REQ-VET-003 (machine-readable directory as a supported surface) is new prose over behavior that already ships, so it carries no slice of its own; the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. For system-design-expert: add the index row for the new ADR to docs/adr/README.md, which is outside this agent's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice extends the existing vet feature package along its current shape: a derived Spring Data query on VetRepository, a query parameter bound by VetController, no new package and no service layer. Two rules the slice needs are not recorded anywhere, which is what makes this new ground rather than a minor adjustment, and each is now an ADR back-linked from system-design.md Persistence. First, case folding happens in the query, not the schema: specialties.name is a plain VARCHAR/TEXT on all three vendors, so plain equality would match case-sensitively under H2 and PostgreSQL and case-insensitively under MySQL, reproducing exactly the divergence that made owner search defective under PostgreSQL. Second, the filtered reads are NOT annotated @Cacheable: the vets cache has no eviction and no size limit, and a caller-supplied specialty would turn its closed key space into an open one on an application with no authentication. Filter in the repository, never in memory in the controller: in-memory filtering after findAll(pageable) would page over the unfiltered list and break the acceptance criterion that paging runs over the narrowed list, and filtering after an unpaged findAll() would put a business rule in a controller, which architecture-principles.md forbids as a fresh violation. The JSON surface's promotion to supported (REQ-VET-003) changes no structure: the route, the Vets wrapper, and the content-negotiation shape all stay as they are. What it changes is durable memory, already written: the Known Defects row calling that route requirement-less is retired, and Vets, VetRepository, and VetController now carry REQ-VET-003 in the Contracts table. The one consequence to respect is compatibility: the unfiltered /vets document shape must not change, so the filter is purely additive.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived reads over the Vet-Specialty join, one paged and one collection-returning, both matching the whole specialty name case-insensitively; neither carries @Cacheable
VetController.showVetList gains an optional specialty request parameter and chooses between the filtered and the existing unfiltered repository call
VetController.showResourcesVetList gains the same optional parameter and fills the existing Vets wrapper from whichever read applies
vetList.html pagination links carry the active specialty forward so paging stays inside the narrowed list
the specialty value is added to the model so the template can rebuild the links; it is never rendered as page text

patterns.description: the existing paged read is the template for the filtered paged read, minus the @Cacheable annotation. Use Spring Data derived queries in the interface's established declarative style: Page<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase(String name, Pageable pageable) and Collection<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase(String name). IgnoreCase emits the vendor-independent case-folded comparison the ADR calls for; the underscore makes the specialties.name property path explicit rather than leaving it to fall back from a non-existent specialtiesName property; Distinct guards the root rows against the ManyToMany join. This is whole-name equality, so no StartingWith or Containing keyword, which is what keeps edge case 3 satisfied and keeps the slice on the filtering side of the NG-9 boundary

blank-parameter normalization to copy for edge case 5. Owner search strips the value and treats null-or-empty as the broadest search; do the same here, declaring the parameter @RequestParam(required = false) and delegating to the existing unfiltered repository call when the stripped value is null or empty. Routing the absent case through the untouched original path is what literally satisfies the criterion that no specialty asked for behaves as it did before narrowing existed. Do not push the branch into the query with a nullable predicate: it would force the join on every unfiltered request and change the REQ-VET-001 path

the pagination links currently build URLs with Thymeleaf's __${i}__ preprocessing. Switch that block to the link-parameter form, @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}, on every link in it. Thymeleaf omits a null parameter, so an unfiltered page renders exactly the URLs it renders today, and it URL-encodes the value, so the reflected parameter cannot break out of the attribute

@WebMvcTest with MockMvc is the sanctioned controller-test shape and the existing @MockitoBean VetRepository stub is the established pattern in this file; stub the new methods in setup() alongside the existing findAll stubs. Assert the filtered cases on the model attribute listVets and on the JSON body rather than on Mockito verify, so the tests state behavior. theVetListShouldPageOverTheFilteredVets needs its stub to return a PageImpl whose total exceeds the page size, so the assertion is that totalPages reflects the narrowed list

risks.risk: copying @Cacheable onto the new repository methods, which is the natural move when extending an interface where both existing reads carry it. The specialty is caller-supplied and the vets cache has no eviction and no size limit, so every invented string would become a resident entry on an application with no authentication
risks.mitigation: the filtered methods carry no cache annotation; ADR 2026-08-04-uncached-filtered-vet-reads records why, and system-design.md Persistence states the rule so a reviewer seeing the asymmetry finds the reason

risks.risk: filtering in memory after findAll() because it is the shortest path to a green JSON test. It would page over the unfiltered list on the HTML surface and would place a selection rule in a controller, which architecture-principles.md § Validation Checklist counts as a fresh Web-controller violation not covered by the existing deviation
risks.mitigation: both surfaces call a repository method that filters; the controller only chooses which method to call, which is request adaptation, not a business rule

risks.risk: adding user-facing text to vetList.html, such as a specialty picker, a 'filtered by' caption, or a 'no veterinarians found' message. Any new message key must exist in all eleven bundles or I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails the build, and edge case 4 explicitly forbids a nothing-found message
risks.mitigation: the template change is confined to the pagination links; no new message key, no new visible text, and an empty result renders the ordinary page with an empty table

risks.risk: echoing the specialty back into the page. The application escapes by default, but th:utext or a JavaScript context would make this a reflected-XSS vector on an unauthenticated route
risks.mitigation: the value reaches the template only as a link parameter, which Thymeleaf URL-encodes; it is never rendered as text

risks.risk: the ManyToMany join yielding duplicate Vet rows and corrupting the page count
risks.mitigation: Distinct in the derived name; the seeded specialty names are unique and PostgreSQL's join table is uniquely constrained, so the guard is cheap insurance rather than a live defect

risks.risk: a filtered page paging over rows the filter did not select, because the eager specialties collection interacts badly with SQL pagination
risks.mitigation: low: findAll(Pageable) already pages this exact eager association, so the machinery is proven. theVetListShouldPageOverTheFilteredVets covers it

notes: Durable memory written this dispatch: two new ADRs (docs/adr/2026-08-04-query-level-case-folding.md, docs/adr/2026-08-04-uncached-filtered-vet-reads.md) with rules back-linked from docs/system-design.md § Persistence; the Contracts rows for Vets, VetRepository, and VetController now carry REQ-VET-003; the Known Defects row calling the machine-readable vet route requirement-less is retired with a dated note; Open Question 5 now points at the cache-key ADR. The ADR index row for docs/adr/2026-08-04-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md that product-requirements-expert could not write is added to docs/adr/README.md, along with rows for both new ADRs. REQ-VET-004 is deliberately not yet written into the Contracts table's Implements column: system-design.md carries current state, and the filter does not exist yet — that belongs to doc-sync after the slice lands. Vocabulary: use Veterinarian in prose and vet in code per docs/ubiquitous-language.md, and never call the Vets wrapper a domain concept. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. The covering-code claims here were resolved by reading the vet package sources directly rather than through the IDE oracle, which is not connected in this run.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection: the specialty value reaches the database only through Spring Data derived queries (findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase, Collection and Page overloads). No string-concatenated SQL, no @Query, no EntityManager use is introduced; parameters are bound. Consistent with the system-design threat model's SQL-injection row.

Reflected XSS: the caller-supplied specialty is placed in the model but never rendered as page text. Its only render site is the Thymeleaf link-expression parameter (@{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}), which URL-encodes the value, and the resulting th:href attribute is HTML-escaped by Thymeleaf's default output escaping (not disabled anywhere). A sweep of src/main/resources/templates for th:utext and for every 'specialty' occurrence in vets/vetList.html found no unescaped sink.

Cache key space: ADR 2026-08-04-uncached-filtered-vet-reads holds in the code as built. A grep of src/main/java for @Cacheable confirms the annotation appears only on the two pre-existing unfiltered VetRepository.findAll methods; neither caller-string-keyed filtered read carries it, so the unbounded, unevicted 'vets' cache is not opened to attacker-chosen keys on this unauthenticated app.

Conditional paging links: ADR 2026-08-04-filter-preserving-paging-links holds. All five link sites render the plain URL when the model attribute is null, so an unnarrowed list emits the pre-existing URLs and no empty specialty= parameter; regression test theUnfilteredVetListPagingLinksShouldCarryNoSpecialty asserts it.

Input normalization: narrowedTo() treats absent, empty, and whitespace-only values as no filter and strips the value before it reaches the query, so no blank-string filter path exists. No new authorization, redirect, file-I/O, deserialization, or logging sink is introduced; the JSON route returns the same Vet shape as before, narrowed.
Secrets: the diff introduces no credential, token, key, or connection-string literal. The only new strings are specialty names in tests and fixtures.

Supply chain: no dependency delta. build.gradle, settings.gradle, and gradle/ are unmodified in the change set, so no new or upgraded coordinate enters the graph; the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in this project, and the review adds no dependency requiring it.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Re-verified against the pass-1 approval (line 17): no production Java, template, or build file changed this round. git diff over src/main/java and src/main/resources/templates is byte-identical to the surface approved in pass 1; the only code-side delta is in the two test files, and docs/system-design.md.

Uncached filtered reads still hold: VetRepository.findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase(String) and its paged overload carry @Transactional(readOnly = true) and no @Cacheable. Only findAll()/findAll(Pageable) remain @Cacheable("vets"), so no caller-supplied string ever becomes a key in the unbounded, unevicted vets cache on this unauthenticated app.

Reflected specialty still escaped: vetList.html renders the value only inside Thymeleaf link expressions (@{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}) in th:href attributes, which URL-encode the parameter and HTML-escape the attribute. Swept the whole templates tree for unescaped output — no th:utext occurs anywhere, and specialty is never emitted as page text via [[...]]. The null-vs-blank branch (th:with narrowed) selects the plain URL when nothing is narrowed, so no attacker-supplied value reaches the unnarrowed link form either.

Injection: the filter reaches the database through a Spring Data derived query method, which binds the name as a JPA parameter. No JPQL/SQL string is built from the request; case folding is done by the query (IgnoreCase), not by string manipulation. VetController.narrowedTo only strips and null-checks, adding no unsafe transformation.

Doc change is contract-only and now matches the code: the system-design Contracts rows cite REQ-VET-004 and the VetRepository row states "only the unfiltered results are cached", which is the property verified in the source. The Persistence and Presentation rules and their ADR back-links state the two security-relevant decisions once each, consistent with the implementation.

Tests introduce no security surface: no hardcoded credentials or secrets (swept the test diff for password/secret/token/api-key/credential/private-key patterns — no hits), no new I/O, no disabled escaping. The new assertions exercise the specialty parameter through MockMvc only.
Supply chain unchanged: no build.gradle, pom, or dependency-declaring file appears in the change set, so the dependency graph verified in pass 1 is untouched and no new CVE surface was introduced.
